title: Compute-path scout: adaptive kernel autotuner with phase probing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build an adaptive compute-path scout that picks the most cost- and latency-efficient implementation for each request class (by arch and sequence-length phase) while keeping tail-latency safety. Background: current static selection misses multi-phase requests (long prefill, short decode) and heterogeneous hardware. Approach: 1) lightweight per-request fingerprinting at prefill boundary (tensor shapes, batch size, seqlen histogram, model variant, token-phase marker); 2) phase probe microbenchmark: run a low-overhead timing probe on a tiny warmup kernel to estimate occupancy/latency trade-offs; 3) surrogate cost model (online ridge + exponential decay) maps fingerprint -> expected p50/p95/p99 and token-cost; 4) decision layer picks an implementation bundle (attention tiling variant + fused-ops, KV layout, quantized path) with exploration epsilon decay and safety bounding; 5) compile-cache warmstart for newly chosen combos, with background JIT and graceful fallback to baseline implementation on compile failures. We will integrate telemetry hooks (per-request trace id) so can link to Console traces and cost dashboards. Rollout plan: gated canary (1%, 5%, 20%) with automatic rollback if p95 increases > 10% or cost-per-token regresses > 8% over baseline window. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, GPU occupancy, kernel time breakdown, cost-per-1000-tokens. Deliverables: runtime decision module, probe harness, surrogate trainer, dashboard tiles, canary automation, test-suite and perf harness.
acceptance_criteria: New decision module makes deterministic choices for >95% of traffic after warmstart window and logs fingerprints
Canary run at 5% for 24h without p95 tail regression >10% and with cost-per-token improvement >3% on mixed test workload
End-to-end perf harness reproduces p50/p95 within 5% of production canary for five model-seqlen pairs
Fallbacks trigger and maintain correctness for any compile or kernel failure within 200ms and incur less than 5% additional latencies in failure mode
